[b]September 26-28, 2027: The Silent Coup of 2027[/b]

Following the pushback from the grand assembly and the seeming willingness of the Chief Consul  Alexandrii-Porgyros IV and Second Consul Phillipe Belgarde to roll over for the assembly, thereby frustrating the plans of the SCSID, the SCSID would quietly move to put into place the Strømm Plan.

With Polenne Strømm out of the country on a diplomatic visit to Flousechia, the SCSID would be able to take advantage of the gap in the triumvirate to summon through the SCSIDs extralegal powers, the PDC and the Republican Central Committee into an extraordinary meeting without the two consuls present.

It was here that General Adolphus Menkins  laid out the flaws and alleged crimes of the 29th triumvirate, namely, failure to maintain the national budget within reasonable constraints, leading to strain on the government purse and on the functions of the government.

Adolphus then made a motion to dissolve the 29th triumvirate and under the extraordinary law, along with the precepts of the Strømm Doctrine whereby the SCSID was compelled to [i]commit to whatever action necessary to defend Rosenmarkket interests, without the need to inform those within the assembly before acting.[/i]

Following a tense vote in the RCC, the vote to dissolve the triumvirate came in narrowly at 7 for and 5 against, with the Patriotic Defense Committee abstaining. 

The vote having been taken quietly gave the SCSID full empowerment to assume temporary executive status, with Menkins becoming the guard of the state in lieu of the absence of the council. As a result, the SCSID moved quickly to ensure compliance and awareness of the dissolution, quietly arresting the former chief and the second consuls the night of the 26th. 

As the morning of the 27th came about, the SCSID moved to take the country dark, using various internal orders sent to broadcasting, internet, and other external-facing services. They silently shut off all non-military communications and inflows. Menkins, having at this point informed Strømm of the dissolution now convened another extraordinary legislative session to announce the news of the dissolution, and explain the reasoning for why the internet and other communications had been cut.

Notably this sparked outrage among the legislators of the assembly who in protest stormed out of the hall and into the streets to publicly inform the citizens of the trespass upon the constitution and the state, though loyalists to the regime, namely those members of the United Triumviral Front, remained to support Menkins.

Almost immediately following the public outcry by those of the Party Populaire, protests would begin in the capitol as the SCSID moved quickly to order the national armed forces onto the streets to maintain order, with Menkins declaring a temporary period of martial law, it had become clear to him that the SCSID had moved far too quickly and had failed to account for the reactions of the citizens.

Thus as evening fell on the 27th and the protests grew, the Menkins moved to dismiss the members of the RCC and order snap-elections. to ensure that the democratic processes remained in place, although media debates had now begun to question whether this was the end of the 5th republic, something which Menkins knew was inevitable.

[b]September 28, 2027: Polenne Strømm becomes Chief Consul[/b]

Word had finally reached Polenne Strømm that the SCSID had undertaken the constitutional initiative to institute the principle of [i]regimeweschel[/i] and initiate a rotation of the triumvirate. She also received word that Rosenmarkket citizens had flooded the streets and were protesting the attempt by the SCSID to institute [i]regimeweschel[/i].

Moving quickly, she departed from the duchy of Montesque, where she had flown to following her visit to Flousechia, and arrived in Rouen-sur-Tŷr, the capital of Rosenmarkke. Upon her arrival, she called to order the heads of the armed forces and the SCSID central council to affirm her commitment to attain the position of chief consul, or duc destat. 

Following this, she made haste to handpick from the assembly two members of the assembly to serve as co-consuls, these being Onnos Hostjn and Mikael Ptolenos, both relatively unknown members of the assembly with a limited voting record, having only been elected to the assembly in the prior elections. 

Finally, appearing on an international broadcast, she made a speech to reassure and stabilise potentially worried allies and enemies of Rosenmarkke, citing: Rosenmarkke remains committed to its international obligations and partners during this time of transition, and it is the hope of the new administration of the 30th triumvirate that your faith in our state will be maintained,

After this, Strømm moved quickly to restore public order, restoring international internet and television access, ending the temporary SCSID blackout. Under the orders of Strømm, the SCSID  moved to restore the dismissed RCC members as the provisional heads of the departments until assembly approval could be gained to move new members in.
